title: Scalar square for a generating section of the constant residue kernel
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l and X any scheme. Let O, q and the exact module transport F be as in [def-sfb-internal-completion-section-transport] and [def-sfb-internal-quotient-tower-model]. Suppose a globally generates kernelIdeal(q) on every slice in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators], and d acts on all continuous point sections as multiplication by the chosen uniformizer. For any integral complex P and n>=0, put N=complex(P), I=O[0], B=Tot(N tensor I), U:B≅N the right unitor, and r=Tot(1 tensor single(a^(n+1))) as defined by [lem-sfb-ringed-singleton-koszul-cone] using [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. There is an isomorphism b:N≅B satisfying F(scalar(d,n,P)) followed by U.inv = b.hom followed by r, with scalar as in [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus]. This is a square between scalar endomorphisms, with a fixed target change of basis; it asserts no mapping-cone, Koszul-dual, or tensor-summand comparison.

source.place: Lemma derived-completion-koszul (0A0E), finite free scalar calculation; integral-models proof (1), constant residue kernel comparison.

proof.text: Obtain the single regular uniformizer section t and its scalar transport equation. Apply regular-generator association to the actual residue kernel and the given generating singleton a. This gives c:O≅O with scalar(t)=c.hom followed by scalar(a).

Rank-one endomorphisms commute, as follows sectionwise by linearity from f(x)=x*f(1) and commutativity of O. Raise the preceding scalar equation to the power n+1, obtaining scalar(t)^(n+1)=c.hom^(n+1) followed by scalar(a)^(n+1).

Set b to the inverse right unitor followed by the tensor functor applied to the degree-zero single-complex image of the automorphism c^(n+1). The Aut-to-End homomorphism identifies its hom with c.hom^(n+1). Use functoriality twice to transport the power factorization into the definition of ringedSingletonKoszulPower, then substitute the uniformizer transport equation. This proves the square without any remaining goal.

proof_origin.place: Rank-one calculation in Lemma derived-completion-koszul (0A0E); N4 proves generator association and all change-of-basis/power algebra, isolating the constant coefficient normalization.

theorem uniformizer_koszul_scalar_square
    (a : ((ring l E X).obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections)
    (ha : ∀ U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} X,
      IsRingedIdealGeneratingList (ring l E X)
        (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).module
        (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).inclusion U 1
        (fun _ ↦ a.val (op U)))
    (d : End (Mod.regular (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)))
    (hd : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (b : (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E).obj.obj S)
      (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) b).down s =
        Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * b.down s)
    (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ b : complex l E X P ≅
        ((ringedKoszulTensor (ring l E X)).obj (complex l E X P)).obj
          (ringedSiteRingComplex (ring l E X)),
      ((modules l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
          (PrincipalReduction.scalar l E X d n P) ≫
          (ringedKoszulRightUnitIso (ring l E X) (complex l E X P)).inv =
        b.hom ≫ ringedSingletonKoszulPower (ring l E X) a (complex l E X P) n
